add-subtract-20-skill-01.target: I can add two numbers within 20 in my head using strategies such as making a ten, doubles, and doubles plus one.
add-subtract-20-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can add two numbers within 20 in my head using strategies such as making a ten, doubles, and doubles plus one.
add-subtract-20-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Counting on from the first number and including that number (8 + 5 → 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 = 12). Try this: Count on from the next number with fingers or a number line, then teach make-a-ten with ten frames so counting is not needed.

add-subtract-20-skill-02.target: I can subtract within 20 in my head by thinking addition, counting back, or going back through ten.
add-subtract-20-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can subtract within 20 in my head by thinking addition, counting back, or going back through ten.
add-subtract-20-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger one (14 − 6 → 6 − 4 = 2 → 12), or counting back and including the start number. Try this: Ask “What do I add to 6 to make 14?” and model the jump back to 10 and then the rest on a number line.

add-subtract-20-skill-03.target: I can use an addition fact to find related addition and subtraction facts in the same fact family.
add-subtract-20-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can use an addition fact to find related addition and subtraction facts in the same fact family.
add-subtract-20-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking the order of numbers can change in a subtraction fact (14 − 6 = 8 → 6 − 14 = 8). Try this: Build the fact family with a part-part-whole mat; the whole is always first in a subtraction fact.

add-subtract-20-skill-04.target: I can find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation within 20 and tell if an equation is true.
add-subtract-20-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation within 20 and tell if an equation is true.
add-subtract-20-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking the equal sign means “write the answer next” (7 + ___ = 15 → 22). Try this: Read = as “is the same as” and check both sides with cubes or a balance picture.
